items.title: Higher K property: A is an n-type if and only if its (n+1)-fold loop space is contractible

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.2.9 at source lines 423-426: A is an n-type if and only if Omega^{n+1}(A,a) is contractible for all a. The proof (source lines 427-445) is an induction whose inductive step is not formal: after reformulating with the loop-space criterion (line 431) and applying the hypothesis (line 432), the goal mentions Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),refl a) while the available contractibility is at Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),p), so one has to construct an explicit equivalence g between the two loop spaces at different basepoints (lines 435-437), define it by whiskering a path q : p = p with the concatenation composite refl a = p `ct` opp p = p `ct` opp p = refl a (lines 438-440), prove it is an equivalence as a composite of two named equivalences (lines 441-443), and check that it carries refl p to refl(refl a) (line 444). The statement says nothing about this basepoint comparison.
